questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That I was a high quality institution. That it was in a city both geographically and culturally close to Copenhagen.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy. Sometimes it took some time to figure stuff out, but I didn't experience not being able to figure something out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a pre-planned intro-week. It included both social stuff and all sorts of practical information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy (and rather cheap). You just need to apply in time. Read about it on UiO's website.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Well you can really live "on campus", so there isen't really any comparison to be made - but the student village I lived in was as close to living "on campus" as one could get. (This is Europe, not the US or Oxford)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't really remember much of the registration process to be honest. Just make sure to register for courses in the first round - some of the other exchange students didn't get the courses they wanted because, they didn't do that. Just make sure to check your e-mail, and I think you might get a message on your phone too when the first registration opens.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Again, I don't remember.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got everything I signed up for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I wasn't able to register for Norwegian language courses as default in the system, but I know that I would qualify for them as a Danish speaker. I only took English language courses so it wasn't a problem for me, but if you want to take courses taught in Norwegian you might need to write to the University if you can find them on the course registration page.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In general it was very close. Sometimes I might have felt a little lower, but that might also be due to the amount of exchange students on the English level courses I took. That said, I study sociology at UCPH, and the quality of teaching there is rather high, so the comparison might be a bit unfair.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
I felt like level of teaching was slightly lower that at UCPH, but mainly because they some courses used as lot of PhD students. There lecture by Associate professors, professors and the like were around the same quality. 

I feel like I have learned a lot more from the courses at UiO than I do back home. But that is mainly due to other factors, primarily being: more time to study (not as many commitments in Oslo as Copenhagen) and different exams (sit down written exams that incentivize learning the entire curricula, not just essays where one needs to use the curricula two of three lectures).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
STV1560 British Politics and institutions
STV2230 International Security Policy
HIS2980 Mapping Schools of History

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them to be honest, however the seminar (class room focused) teaching in HIS2980 sometimes didn't live up to my expectations when I came to teaching quality.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Food is just more expensive in Norway, but I can't think of something in particular.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Insurance - because I was in Denmark relatively often (work obligations and so on), I didn't need to pay more for travel insurance, since I was never out of Denmark for more than 60 days straight.
Phone and internet - my phone provider gave me the same coverage in Norway as it did in Denmark, and I had enough roaming data, so I never needed to get a norwegian phone number. Internet came free with my housing.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A whole lot, everything basically.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Didn't really use it that much. If you are interested in foreign and defense policy then maybe YATA, but be warned - everything is in Norwegian.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go skiing I guess, not really my thing but it seems like people do that a lot up here.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It's basically Denmark but colder.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them as you would Danes. Alcohol... can I say that???

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not that many to be honest, maybe language if I insisted on speaking Danish, but that was easily fixed by switching to English if there was too much "huh?? :o".

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Again, it's basically Denmark, just a little richer and a little colder.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Bring warm clothes.
At least try to speak Danish and try adding Norwegian words into you Danish.
REMEMBER TO APPLY FOR HOUSING!!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: REMEMBERING TO APPLY FOR HOUSING!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Actually learning a lot (the cold made sitting inside and reading rather attractive).

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The cold - it's bloody cold up here.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
